transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-04-01
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 43 mins (approx)
Attendees: Samira (AE, Redwood), Jordan (SE, Redwood), Priya (SE, Redwood); Ethan (CTO, Ironclad), Maya (Eng Mgr, Ironclad), Ravi (SRE, Ironclad), Olivia (Security, Ironclad)

Summary:
Ironclad Health is evaluating Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPUs) with a likely private/VPC path for HIPAA workloads. They need guidance on isolation/topology, burst handling (hot pool vs pre-warm), eviction tolerance, and KMS/HSM integration for PHI. They asked for cost/latency tradeoffs, examples of fallback routing to hosted models, and a short benchmarking plan.

Topics covered:
- Current inference stack and constraints
- Isolation requirements and auditability (HIPAA + SOC2)
- Burst strategy: warm pool, pre-warming, evictions
- Autoscaling cadence and expected cold start latencies
- Benchmarking and next steps

Transcript body:
[00:00] Samira (AE): hey everyone, thanks for hopping on, should we go around real quick?
[00:07] Ethan (CTO): sure, Ethan Moore here, CTO. We're looking at moving inference for our PHI flows off the in-house cluster, maybe onto Redwood Dedicated or private. main drivers are latency guarantees and auditability.
[00:20] Maya (Eng Mgr): Maya — we own infra and ML platform. big question for us is tenancy/isolation. we need tenant fencing so one customer can't spike someone else's capacity.
[00:30] Samira: totally, that's a common ask — Redwood Dedicated supports reserved GPU pools and tenant fencing patterns. Jordan can walk through topologies in a second.
[00:38] Jordan (SE): yeah hi all. quick map: we usually offer two topologies — single-tenant reserved nodes per customer, which gives strongest isolation and predictable throughput; or shared pools with soft isolation (cgroups/containers + tenant quotas) plus strict eviction and QoS. for HIPAA you'd often pick single-tenant or a VPC private deployment.
[01:02] Ravi (SRE): when you say single-tenant, are we talking physically isolated nodes? like no multi-tenant on the same GPU?
[01:08] Jordan: right — dedicated physical nodes or dedicated GPUs per tenant. we can do node affinity so your tenants are pinned. there's also a hybrid: reserved node with guest isolation for dev/testing.
[01:18] Olivia (Security): we need KMS/HSM integration and full audit logs for model access and token-level tracing. how mature is that?
[01:25] Priya (SE): we integrate with customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS, GCP CMEK) and can surface audit logs via our console and log export. note: some field labels in our older docs say 'audittrail' — apologies for naming inconsistencies. logs include model loads, key requests, and admin actions.
[01:42] Ethan: good. what's the onboarding path for an on-prem or VPC install vs hosted?
[01:47] Samira: two tracks — Hosted to Dedicated (cloud) is quickest: you reserve capacity and we allocate GPU pools in the region. Private/VPC or on-prem is a longer engagement: we ship a private control plane and optionally an on-prem runtime. timeline usually 6-12 weeks for Private depending on networking and compliance.
[02:05] Maya: okay, that fits our window but our real concern is burst traffic. we have unpredictable spikes during end-of-day processing. how do you handle bursts without paying for peak all the time?
[02:16] Jordan: two levers — pre-warmed warm pools and autoscaling with burst buckets. warm pools are small hot nodes kept ready; autoscaling is based on queue depth and can add nodes, but cold starts are non-zero. we also support graceful fallback to smaller/quantized model variants to keep latency.
[02:33] Ravi: what's typical cold start for a 70B model?
[02:36] Jordan: depends on quantization and NVLink setup; ballpark cold start 12–60s if you need to load model weights from disk into GPU. with warm pool pre-warm you can get token latency back to ~30–50ms per token. our metrics vary.
[02:51] Ethan: 12–60s could break customer flows. can we rely on fallback to hosted smaller model? that's a potential graceful degradation path.
[02:58] Priya: yes — smart routing can route to a hosted variant with slightly lower quality but much faster availability. we recommend SLO tiers: gold traffic hits reserved nodes, silver can fallback to hosted. that reduces reserved capacity needed.
[03:11] Maya: for HIPAA data, routing to hosted models might be a no-go unless hosted is within a Private deployment.
[03:17] Samira: correct. for PHI you likely need Private or Dedicated with VPC that keeps data in your network. we can do private control plane and publish logs to your SIEM.
[03:25] Olivia: we need encryption in transit and at rest and key rotation policy. does Redwood support BYOK?
[03:30] Priya: yes BYOK with KMS, rotation policies are supported. we'll share KMS integration doc.
[03:35] Ethan: another thing: our ML stack uses very bursty, short requests with long contexts (medical notes ~4–6k tokens). how does sequencing affect batching and throughput?
[03:45] Jordan: long contexts reduce batching efficiency and increase memory pressure. two options: quantize models and use KV caching for repeated prefixes — we also support continuous batching with sequence-aware routing. caching repeated prefixes saves a lot.
[04:01] Ravi: you mentioned KV cache — i've seen transcripts call it KV cash in older logs — will that be an issue to explain to our auditors.
[04:07] Priya: haha yes transcription oddities. But we'll provide clear design docs. KV cache stores prefix keys in GPU memory to speed up repeated conversations.
[04:17] Maya: about evictions — what's the eviction tolerance? if a pre-warmed node is reclaimed for another tenant during a spike, can requests failover gracefully?
[04:26] Jordan: eviction policy is configurable. you can set eviction to never for critical nodes, but that costs more. another pattern: configure small burstable spare capacity and a queued fallback with timeouts. we have a fallback policy that reroutes to a lower-cost region or model variant.
[04:40] Ethan: sounds good. what's the pricing model for warm pools? is it hourly reserved + consumption?
[04:46] Samira: reserved capacity is a monthly commit for nodes; warm pools can be sized as part of that or be a small hourly burst-add. we'll send a worksheet with examples showing reserved + warm pool + burst rates.
[04:58] Olivia: compliance question — can we get a pen test/report for the private runtime?
[05:03] Priya: yes we have pen test summaries and SOC2 reports; for Private we can do an extra security review and provide attestations.
[05:09] Ethan: okay, can you outline the benchmark plan you suggested? we want a cheap short-run test to validate latency and eviction behavior.
[05:15] Jordan: proposed: 48-hour window with a small reserved pool (2 nodes) and a warm pool (1 node) plus scripted synthetic traffic reflecting your token distribution and 10% surge events. we'll capture per-token latency, cold-start times, evictions, and cost. we'll also test fallback routing to hosted smaller model.
[05:32] Maya: will Redwood run the benchmark or we run it?
[05:35] Samira: we can coordinate — Redwood will provide the guide and run it with your telemetry; you'll provide sample payloads and an account to run in a sandbox.
[05:43] Ravi: network egress — we need to know if there's any cross-region traffic egress cost if fallback routes to hosted.
[05:49] Priya: we'll include egress considerations in the worksheet. we usually recommend collocating warm pools in same region.
[05:55] Ethan: competitor question, has anyone compared this to Anthropic or Cohere on similar workloads?
[06:00] Jordan: yes clients often evaluate Anthropic and Cohere; key diffs are model variants, and how each provider handles private deployments and warm pools. Redwood is focused on production economics and private deployments; we'll share a short competitive note.
[06:12] Olivia: one more security note — audit trail needs to be immutable and exportable to our Splunk. can you export in a compatible format?
[06:19] Priya: yes JSONL or syslog push; we can integrate with Splunk or your SIEM via secure forwarder.
[06:26] Ethan: timeline — if we like the benchmarking results, how fast could we move to a Private deployment?
[06:31] Samira: typical is 6–12 weeks. if you sign a pilot agreement sooner we can prioritize a 6-week track.
[06:37] Maya: ok budget wise we need a ballpark cost for 2 reserved nodes + 1 warm pool and burst to 6 nodes during peak.
[06:44] Samira: we'll model that in the worksheet. approximate numbers, then refine after your benchmark.
[06:51] Ravi: about monitoring — can we get token-level cost breakouts per route?
[06:55] Jordan: yes console shows per-route token latency, cost breakdown, and model-level traces.
[07:00] Maya: small nit — we use Terraform for infra. does Redwood provide IaC modules for Dedicated/VPC?
[07:06] Priya: yes we have Terraform modules and a deployment guide; we'll link those.
[07:11] Ethan: ok great. any final clarifications?
[07:14] Olivia: please redact any sample data on our side when running benchmarks — we will provide synthetic copies.
[07:19] Samira: understood. we'll treat sample payloads carefully.
[07:22] Samira: recap — action items and next steps then we'll wrap.
[07:26] Samira: Jordan — you will produce the mini-benchmark guide; Samira will send pricing worksheet; Priya + Olivia will schedule security deep dive; customer to provide sample payloads and expected surge profiles.
[07:36] Ethan: yep. thanks everyone.
[07:38] Maya: thanks.
[07:40] End of call.
